message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1","text":"After James had read the letter, he summoned the elders, and after reading it to them he said, “Necessarily and fittingly, our Peter has reminded us to take precautions concerning the truth, so that we should not pass on indiscriminately to anyone the books of his proclamations that have been sent to us, but only to someone good and devout, one who chooses to teach and is a circumcised believer. And we should not pass on all of them at once, so that if he is discovered to be untrustworthy with the first, he will not be entrusted with the later ones. Therefore, let him be tested for no fewer than six years. Then, after bringing him in accordance with the way of Moses to a river or a spring—which is ‘living water,’ where the rebirth of the righteous takes place—do not make him swear an oath, since that is not permitted. Instead, command him to stand beside the water and make a solemn attestation, just as we ourselves did when we were commanded to do so as we were being reborn, for the sake of not sinning.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὡς ἔτυχεν","chosen":"indiscriminately","rationale":"The idiom means without careful selection, rather than merely by chance."},{"source_quote":"ἐνπεριτόμῳ τε ὄντι πιστῷ","chosen":"is a circumcised believer","rationale":"Takes ἐνπεριτόμῳ adjectivally of the qualified recipient without altering the supplied form."},{"source_quote":"ἀγνώμων","chosen":"untrustworthy","rationale":"In the context of testing a recipient’s handling of restricted books, this conveys deficient judgment or reliability better than the narrower ‘ungrateful.’"},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τὴν Μωϋσέως ἀγωγὴν","chosen":"in accordance with the way of Moses","rationale":"ἀγωγή denotes a prescribed way, discipline, or practice here."},{"source_quote":"ἐπιμαρτύρασθαι","chosen":"make a solemn attestation","rationale":"The verb introduces the formal invocation of witnesses stated in the following passage without making the act an oath."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"2","text":"And let him say: “May I have as witnesses heaven, earth, and water, in which all things are contained, and besides all these also the air that permeates everything, without which I do not breathe, that I will always be obedient to the one who gives me the books of the proclamations, and that, as for my books themselves, whichever he may give me, I will certainly not pass them on to anyone in any way: not by writing them out, not by giving away what has been written, not by handing them over to someone who is writing; not myself, not through another person, not through any other course of action or deception or device; not by guarding them carelessly, or leaving them somewhere, or giving a signal, or by any other method or scheme passing them on to someone else. The only exception is if I test someone and find him worthy—as I myself was judged, or after testing him even more extensively, though for no fewer than six years. Then I will hand them on, just as I received them, to a devout and good person who will undertake to teach, and I will do this with the approval of my bishop.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"αὐτάς μου τὰς βίβλους, ἃς ἂν μοι δῷ","chosen":"as for my books themselves, whichever he may give me","rationale":"Preserves both the possessive μου and the emphasis of αὐτάς, while ἃς ἂν is represented by the open-ended ‘whichever.’"},{"source_quote":"οὐ μὴ μεταδῶ","chosen":"I will certainly not pass them on","rationale":"The paired negatives emphatically deny any future disclosure."},{"source_quote":"οὐ γράψας, οὐ γεγραμμένον δούς, οὐ γράφοντι ἀναδιδούς","chosen":"not by writing them out, not by giving away what has been written, not by handing them over to someone who is writing","rationale":"Preserves the three distinct prohibited routes of copying, distributing written material, and supplying it to a copyist."},{"source_quote":"ἢ τιθῶν ἢ νεύων","chosen":"or leaving them somewhere, or giving a signal","rationale":"Preserves the terse actions without specifying an unstated recipient or purpose."},{"source_quote":"πλεῖον δοκιμάσας","chosen":"after testing him even more extensively","rationale":"πλεῖον may concern greater duration or rigor; ‘more extensively’ leaves that dimension open."},{"source_quote":"διδάσκειν ἐπαναρουμένῳ","chosen":"who will undertake to teach","rationale":"The supplied form is analyzed as a future-middle participle of ἐπαναίρω. In context it prospectively describes taking up or undertaking the work of teaching."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τῇ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου μου γνώμῃ","chosen":"with the approval of my bishop","rationale":"γνώμη here denotes the bishop’s judgment or consent governing the transfer."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3","text":"“Otherwise, not even a child or a brother or a friend or anyone in any other way ever related to me, if indeed he is unworthy—for this one’s sake not to pass it on, since it is not proper. I will not fear a plot, nor will I be won over by gifts. But even if at some point the books of the proclamations given to me seem to me not to be true, not even then will I pass them on; instead, I will return them. When traveling, I will carry with me whichever of them I happen to possess. But if I do not wish to carry them about with me, I will not leave them in my house; instead, I will entrust them for safekeeping to my bishop, who holds the same faith and proceeds from the same starting points. If I should also happen to become ill and anticipate death, if I am childless, I will do likewise. But even if I die leaving a child who is unworthy or not yet capable, I will do likewise, for I will entrust them for safekeeping to my bishop, so that if the child, after reaching maturity, should happen to be worthy of the faith, the bishop will return them to the child as a paternal deposit, in accordance with the terms of the solemn attestation.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἄλλως δὲ οὐδ’ ἂν τέκνον ἢ ἀδελφὸς ἢ φίλος ἢ ἄλλως πως ποτὲ γένους μοι ἀνήκων, ἐάνπερ ἀνάξιος ᾖ, τοῦδε μὴ μεταδοῦναι χάριν, ὡς οὐ προσῆκεν","chosen":"Otherwise, not even a child or a brother or a friend or anyone in any other way ever related to me, if indeed he is unworthy—for this one’s sake not to pass it on, since it is not proper","rationale":"The rendering remains formally fragmentary rather than supplying an unattested governing verb. It provisionally groups τοῦδε with χάριν as ‘for this one’s sake,’ while the unresolved syntax and alternative reference of τοῦδε remain disclosed in source_issues."},{"source_quote":"οὔτε ἐπιβουλὴν φοβηθήσομαι","chosen":"I will not fear a plot","rationale":"ἐπιβουλή denotes a hostile design or plot rather than fear in general."},{"source_quote":"ἀποδημῶν","chosen":"when traveling","rationale":"The participle describes being away on a journey without specifying a particular destination."},{"source_quote":"εἰ δὲ μὴ βουληθῶ μεθ’ ἑαυτοῦ αὐτὰ περιφέρειν","chosen":"if I do not wish to carry them about with me","rationale":"The reflexive ἑαυτοῦ is understood contextually with the first-person subject; this usage does not require alteration to ἐμαυτοῦ."},{"source_quote":"παρακαταθήσομαι","chosen":"I will entrust them for safekeeping","rationale":"The middle verb describes depositing property with another person as a trust."},{"source_quote":"ἀπὸ τῶν αὐτῶν ὁρμωμένῳ","chosen":"proceeds from the same starting points","rationale":"Preserves the source’s metaphor of setting out from shared principles."},{"source_quote":"ἄξιος εἶναι τῆς πίστεως","chosen":"to be worthy of the faith","rationale":"πίστις most naturally denotes the shared faith in this ecclesial context, though ‘trust’ remains semantically possible."},{"source_quote":"πατρῴαν παρακαταθήκην","chosen":"a paternal deposit","rationale":"Preserves the legal image of property entrusted for later restoration as something received from the child’s father."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἄλλως δὲ οὐδ’ ἂν τέκνον ἢ ἀδελφὸς ἢ φίλος ἢ ἄλλως πως ποτὲ γένους μοι ἀνήκων, ἐάνπερ ἀνάξιος ᾖ, τοῦδε μὴ μεταδοῦναι χάριν, ὡς οὐ προσῆκεν","issue":"The construction lacks a securely identifiable governing predicate for the nominative persons and does not establish a clear relation among τοῦδε, μὴ μεταδοῦναι, and χάριν. The translation provisionally takes τοῦδε with χάριν as referring to the unworthy person, but τοῦδε could instead refer to what is transmitted, and other regroupings remain possible. No complete English reconstruction is secure without supplying or reassigning syntax.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"εἰ δὲ μὴ βουληθῶ μεθ’ ἑαυτοῦ αὐτὰ περιφέρειν","issue":"The reflexive ἑαυτοῦ has a first-person referent supplied by βουληθῶ and the surrounding first-person discourse. This is treated as a possible reflexive usage, not as evidence of textual corruption.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"παρακαταθήσομαι·,","issue":"The selected edition prints a middle dot immediately followed by a comma. This is an editorial punctuation anomaly and does not affect the clause’s meaning.","proposed_reading":"παρακαταθήσομαι,","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"4","text":"“As assurance that I will do so, I once again, for a second time, call as witnesses heaven, earth, and water, in which all things are contained, and besides all these also the air that permeates everything, without which I do not breathe, that I will always be obedient to the one who gives me the books of the proclamations, and I will observe in every respect everything I solemnly attested, or even something more. Therefore, if I keep the agreements, I will have a share with the holy ones; but if I act contrary to what I agreed, may the whole universe be hostile to me, as well as the ether that permeates everything and the God who is above all, than whom no one is better, than whom no one is greater. But even if I come to entertain the supposition of another god, I now swear by that one too that I will not act otherwise, whether he exists or does not exist. Besides all this, if I lie, I will be accursed while alive and after death, and I will be punished with eternal punishment.” After this, let him partake of bread and salt with the one who hands the books on.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πάλιν τὸ δεύτερον","chosen":"once again, for a second time","rationale":"Preserves the source’s emphatic repetition rather than reducing it to a single temporal expression."},{"source_quote":"ἢ καί τι πλεῖον","chosen":"or even something more","rationale":"Preserves the unqualified additional undertaking without introducing an uncertainty marker."},{"source_quote":"φυλάσσοντι οὖν μοι τὰς συνθήκας","chosen":"if I keep the agreements","rationale":"συνθῆκαι are the solemnly accepted terms or agreements established by the attestation."},{"source_quote":"ὁ διὰ πάντων διήκων αἰθὴρ","chosen":"the ether that permeates everything","rationale":"Renders αἰθήρ distinctly from the earlier ἀήρ, ‘air,’ while preserving the image of permeation."},{"source_quote":"εἰς ἑτέρου θεοῦ ὑπόνοιαν γένωμαι","chosen":"if I come to entertain the supposition of another god","rationale":"ὑπόνοια can denote supposition or suspicion; the rendering leaves the precise epistemic force open while preserving the hypothetical claim."},{"source_quote":"κἀκεῖνον νῦν ὄμνυμι","chosen":"I now swear by that one too","rationale":"The accusative with ὄμνυμι identifies the additional being invoked in the declaration."},{"source_quote":"κατάθεμα ἔσομαι ζῶν καὶ θανὼν","chosen":"I will be accursed while alive and after death","rationale":"Preserves ἔσομαι as a future assertion and distinguishes it from the preceding optative εἴη, while representing the contrast between living and having died."},{"source_quote":"αἰωνίῳ κολασθήσομαι κολάσει","chosen":"I will be punished with eternal punishment","rationale":"The future indicative is retained as an asserted consequence rather than recast as a wish."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"5","text":"After James said these things, the elders turned pale with anguish. Seeing that they had become very afraid, James said, “Listen to me, brothers and fellow servants. If we make the books available to everyone indiscriminately and they are adulterated by certain daring men or distorted by interpretations, as you have already heard that some have done, the result will be that even those who truly seek the truth will thereafter continually go astray. Therefore, it is better for the books to remain with us and for us to pass them on, with every safeguard previously mentioned, to those who wish to live devoutly and save others. But if anyone, after making such a solemn attestation, acts otherwise, he will justly fall under eternal punishment. For on what grounds will someone who has become responsible for the destruction of others not himself be destroyed?” The elders were pleased with James’s judgment and said, “Blessed is the one who, foreknowing all things, appointed you well as bishop for us.” And when they had said these things, we rose and prayed to the Father and God of all: “To whom is the glory throughout the ages. Amen.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὠχρίασαν ἀγωνιάσαντες","chosen":"turned pale with anguish","rationale":"Preserves both their visible pallor and the distress that caused it."},{"source_quote":"νοθευθῶσιν","chosen":"are adulterated","rationale":"The verb depicts the books as corrupted by the introduction of spurious material."},{"source_quote":"ταῖς ἑρμηνείαις διαστραφῶσιν","chosen":"distorted by interpretations","rationale":"Preserves both the interpretive means and the resulting distortion; ἑρμηνεῖαι may also encompass explanatory renderings or translations."},{"source_quote":"ἔσται λοιπὸν καὶ τοῖς ὄντως τὴν ἀλήθειαν ζητοῦσιν ἀεὶ πλανᾶσθαι","chosen":"the result will be that even those who truly seek the truth will thereafter continually go astray","rationale":"Expresses the impersonal construction while retaining λοιπὸν and the continuing force of ἀεί."},{"source_quote":"εὐλόγως αἰωνίᾳ ὑποπεσεῖται κολάσει","chosen":"he will justly fall under eternal punishment","rationale":"εὐλόγως marks the punishment as warranted or reasonable, not as verbal praise."},{"source_quote":"Εὐλόγηται ὁ σὲ ὡς πάντα προειδὼς καλῶς ἡμῖν καταστήσας ἐπίσκοπον","chosen":"Blessed is the one who, foreknowing all things, appointed you well as bishop for us","rationale":"Εὐλόγηται is rendered as a perfect passive assertion of a resulting blessed state, not as a wish. The foreknowledge describes the one who made the appointment, and καλῶς evaluates that appointment."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καὶ· αὗται","issue":"The selected edition prints a middle dot immediately after the conjunction καί, interrupting the conjunction from its coordinated pronoun. This is an editorial punctuation feature; the syntax continues with αὗται and does not indicate unresolved textual corruption.","proposed_reading":"καὶ αὗται","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
